title: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
problem: Real-world LLM serving systems lack understanding of actual KVCache access patterns, and cache eviction policies are not optimized for production workloads where design decisions are highly workload-dependent.
motivation: KVCache caching significantly improves LLM serving throughput and latency, which is critical for cloud providers.
method: The paper characterizes KVCache workload patterns from production traces at a leading LLM provider, analyzing reuse distributions across single-turn and multi-turn requests and their temporal properties. Based on observations that reuse time and probability are predictable within specific request categories, they propose a workload-aware cache eviction policy that adapts to these patterns.
key_novelty: First production-based characterization showing KVCache reuses are skewed and single-turn request reuses are equally important as multi-turn requests, contradicting prior synthetic workload assumptions.
contributions: First systematic characterization of KVCache workload patterns from production LLM service provider
Empirical findings that single-turn and multi-turn request KVCache reuses are equally important
Analysis showing reuse time and probability patterns are predictable within request categories
Workload-aware cache eviction policy improving serving performance under limited cache capacity
limitations: Characterization from single cloud provider; generalization to other LLM serving platforms not discussed.
primary_theme: Production-driven KVCache optimization for LLM serving
